potentialConflicts.description: Both specs enhance boredom-manager.ts. Boredom detection spec adds idle detection and activity fetching. Lifecycle automation spec adds template mapping for fetched activities.
potentialConflicts.reasoning: Changes are complementary and non-overlapping. Boredom detection provides infrastructure (fetchBoredomActivities), lifecycle automation uses that infrastructure (maps activity types to meta-templates). They work together.
potentialConflicts.resolution: No action required - changes are designed to work together

potentialConflicts.description: Lifecycle automation depends on bootstrap templates being available. Bootstrap compliance spec ensures templates load from embedded imports without filesystem dependencies.
potentialConflicts.reasoning: Bootstrap compliance spec ensures meta-templates (evolve-activity-self-contained, debug-activity-self-contained) are available. Lifecycle automation spec uses these templates. Dependency is satisfied.
potentialConflicts.resolution: No action required - dependency is satisfied

sharedComponents.recommendation: Changes are complementary. No refactoring needed.

mcpAbstraction.verification: All lifecycle operations use MCP tools (metabob_register_activity_template, metabob_fetch_boredom_activities, activity_error_inspector). No direct HTTP to RPC API.

bootstrapTemplates.verification: Lifecycle automation uses bootstrap templates (evolve-activity-self-contained, debug-activity-self-contained) which are loaded from embedded imports per bootstrap-template-filepath-compliance spec.
